pairs.evidence: scripts/census/check-library-adherence.mjs:10 The adherence checker says an adopted census rule's drift fails `npm run check`, but `check` runs only `census:test` (fixtures) and `library:check`, and nothing in `check` or CI runs `run-census.mjs --check`. The day a rule is adopted in rules.json its ratchet will block nothing, while the label says it is enforced.

techniques.evidence: scripts/census/check-library-adherence.mjs:10 The label claims drift is blocking. Traced through the exit codes, no `check` stage ever runs the census over the real tree.

scripts/census/run-census.mjs:58 The usage names `census:check` as 'the gate', but package.json declares no `census:check` script, and neither `check` nor CI invokes `census`. The gate is bound to nothing.
scripts/census/lib/engine.mjs:271 A walk below the floor, zero matches, a stale exclude and an empty registry are all structural failures, and self-test.mjs:355 asserts that each one fires.
scripts/census/lib/engine.mjs:294 Direction 3: every declared location (an exclude path) must still resolve to a real file, or the run fails.

scripts/census/check-library-adherence.mjs:12 A closed vocabulary (adopted, satisfied, declined, unreviewed) with an explicit 'nobody looked' state, so no cell is left blank.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:732 In `--range` mode (CI over a PR), the trailers are parsed from every commit in the range. Any one unscoped `Doc-sync: <reason>` then dismisses every coupled doc the whole range owes, including findings from commits appended later that the sentence never named.

techniques.evidence: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:732 The fallback to an unnamed blanket waiver gives it range-wide reach. A scoped form exists but is optional.

scripts/sentinel/run.ts:150 An unreadable store or an unevaluable verdict is REFUSED with exit 2 and an all-unevaluable report, never a pass.
scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:46 Each block (A-E) is labelled BLOCKING or informational, and the exit code follows that label.
scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:258 The commit-msg rung reads the staged diff rather than the working tree or a transcript, and never mutates anything.
scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:50 Every map row's doc and sourceGlob must resolve against the tree (direction 3).
scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:10 A doc-coupling convention that existed only as prose was mechanised into a blocking checker.
scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:80 There is a sanctioned escape, and dismissals are counted. Candidate couplings in D are reported, never refused.
scripts/kpi/verify-loop.mjs:16 The meter derives its stage list from the gate's own definition instead of a hand copy.
scripts/kpi/citation-coverage.mjs:64 The meter asks the ESLint engine for the resolved config rather than grepping eslint.config. It also handles layered-config replacement for the labs opt-out.
scripts/kpi/citation-coverage.mjs:36 It states that the lint gate's green covers only presence and measures the 'dated' half separately.
scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:749 The refusal prints the exact scoped trailer, a remedy the author can always write.

pairs.registryProposal: waiver-names-its-finding could name the 'scoped form exists but is optional' variant: offering a per-finding waiver while still honouring an unscoped one keeps the full blanket reach, and the risk grows when trailers are collected across a PR range rather than one commit.
